  "text": "The baby monitor began picking up a man counting backward.

“Forty-three. Forty-two. Forty-one.”

I checked the nursery. Ella slept with one fist tucked beneath her cheek. The window was locked.

Downstairs, the counting stopped.

I unplugged the monitor.

“Forty,” it said.

My husband worked nights. I called him, but someone answered before the first ring.

“Don't bring anyone else into this,” the man said.

I ran upstairs and lifted Ella from her crib.

The monitor crackled in my hand, though I'd left it on the kitchen counter.

“Thirty-nine.”

I carried her outside. Every house on our street was dark except ours. In the nursery window, someone stood holding a baby.

I looked down.

Ella opened her eyes.

“Don't look at him,” she said.

She was seven months old.

Across the street, Mrs. Vale opened her front door. She wore a coat over her nightdress and held a little yellow shoe.

“How far has he got?” she asked.

“Thirty-nine.”

“Then there's time. Put her back.”

The thing in my arms gripped my collar.

Inside our house, a baby began to cry.

Mrs. Vale crossed the road and turned down the blanket. Around the small ankle was a hospital band bearing my name.

Not Ella's. Mine.

“I kept you,” she whispered. “Your mother begged me not to, but I kept you.”

The nursery window slid open.

“Thirty-eight,” the man called.

Mrs. Vale pressed the yellow shoe into my hand.

It fit the bare foot sticking out of the blanket.

Upstairs, the crying stopped. The man stepped back from the window.

I tightened my hold and carried the baby inside."
